newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow dip dampens Australia stocks mood at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow dip dampens Australia stocks mood at open.

text.p: The Australian share market softened at the open on Wednesday after Wall Street's optimism was tempered by an inflation warning from the U.S. Federal Reserve.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index fell 7.1 points to 2,248.8. The September share price index futures lost eight points to 2,256, a 7.2 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said the waning of Wall Street's recent rally and softening sentiment towards resource stocks had combined to send the bourse to lower ground.
"The leaders are all off but the resources have taken most of the fall," said a Sydney-based dealer.
Noting substantial falls in miner CRA, he said resources seemed to be at the top of investor's current worry list.
"CRA dropped early and they are due to report tomorrow but everyone seems to be worried about resources at the moment," the dealer said.
Turnover levels remained modest with little corporate activity to galvanise players into action.
